**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 24 of the Cobalt Cloud agreement already delivers our preferred ASSIGN position on all three limbs:

| Playbook requirement | Where satisfied |
|---|---|
| Customer may assign to Affiliate/M&A successor without consent | **24.1** — consent-free, notice-only, assignee assumes obligations |
| Vendor may not assign without our consent; never to a competitor | **24.2** — covers assignment, delegation of material performance, *and* transfer by change of control; reasonableness standard; absolute competitor bar |
| No Vendor rights on Customer's change of control | **24.4** — no termination, suspension, re-pricing, Fee acceleration, or service reduction; Vendor must cooperate with successor administration |

Two points from the planner hints checked and cleared:

- **24.3 does not undercut 24.1.** It opens with "For other assignments," so it governs only transfers falling outside the 24.1 carve-out, and it operates mutually with a not-unreasonably-withheld/conditioned/delayed standard.
- **13.3 tracks Section 24.** Licence transfer rights run to an Affiliate or successor "in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24," so the licence follows the entity without a separate consent gate.

A document-wide sweep for "change of control," "assign," and deemed-assignment language found no hidden Vendor exit or re-pricing trigger. The only other assignment reference is the mutual insolvency clause in 9.2, which expressly carves out lawful reorganizations that do not impair performance — so it cannot be used as a back-door change-of-control termination right against us.
